subject: Histogram - from qplot syntax to layers syntax

messages.author: ada445e3a439dd38
messages.subject: Histogram - from qplot syntax to layers syntax
parts:
Hi,

I've recently started with ggplot2 and I have been using it more and
more.
Thanks for such a great library.

I have been using qplot to plot a histogram of a dataframe with the
following command.
d$count holds the frequencies since my data has already been
"tabulated".

qplot(
d$links,
data=d,
weight=d$count,
geom="histogram",
binwidth = 1
) +
scale_x_continuous() +
scale_y_continuous() +
labs(x = "links", y = "counts")

Now I have a second dataframe (d2) and would like to use ggplot to
combine two layers in the same plot.
Something like:

ggplot() +
layer(
data=d,
mapping = aes(x=d$links),
weight=d$count,
geom="histogram",
binwidth = 1
) +
scale_x_continuous() +
scale_y_continuous() +
labs(x = "links", y = "counts")

But this isn't working correctly. It seems that weight is not being
set for the histogram.

Thanks in advance for any comments on this issue,
--
Sérgio Nunes

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: Histogram - from qplot syntax to layers syntax
parts:
Hi,

I think you want something like this,

qplot(links, data=d, weight=count, geom="histogram", binwidth = 1) +
geom_histogram(data=d2, fill="red", binwidth = 1) +

where geom_histogram() adds a new layer to the plot.

Note that because you specify a data.frame to ggplot or qplot, you
don't need to (and shouldn't) use the $ operator when setting
aesthetics or parameters.

HTH,

baptiste

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Histogram - from qplot syntax to layers syntax
parts:
> Since my initial posting I found an error on my code.
> On the layer definition, "weight" should be enclosed within the "aes"
> definition: [...] mapping = aes(x=d$links, weight=d$count), [...]

You never want to use $ in the aes call - you want the specification
to be independent of the name of the data frame you're currently
using.

Hadley
